page: Amazon Web Services r8a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R45 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs without multithreading overhead, operating at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, with hardware support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and bfloat16 vector extensions.

The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per core). In synthetic memory benchmarks, it delivers uncached large-block read bandwidth of 218.68 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 136.6 GB/sec. Baseline network performance is rated at 15 Gbps. The r8a.8xlarge does not include local instance storage, requiring workloads to rely on remote storage solutions such as Amazon EBS.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top 10% for single-core execution (Geekbench single-core score of 2834.0) and multi-core processing (Geekbench multi-core score of 27850.0). It demonstrates exceptional throughput in database operations and data decompression, alongside high Redis performance reaching 103.4 million operations per second. Additionally, support for AVX-512 and VNNI contributes to strong small-to-medium parameter CPU-based LLM inference rates.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high DDR5 memory density and single-thread-per-core layout eliminate hyperthreading contention, maximizing predictable compute yields per gigabyte of memory allocated. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local NVMe storage and lack of discrete hardware accelerators. AWS r8a.8xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching tiers like Redis or Memcached, big data analytics engines, and CPU-based vector inference.
description: Amazon Web Services r8a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC 9R45 processors clocked up to 4.5 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides 256.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation without multithreading contention. Networking offers a baseline throughput of 15 Gbps, while local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs are absent, requiring external network-attached volumes. Benchmark data shows top-tier results in single-core tasks, PassMark database execution, and multi-threaded compilation, paired with solid memory bandwidth figures reaching 218.68 GB/sec for uncached reads. This hardware profile makes the r8a.8xlarge an efficient platform for memory-bound workloads, including distributed in-memory caches, relational database systems, memory-intensive analytics, and CPU-driven machine learning inference pipelines.
